newsitem.title: CHINA: China says own refiners flout diesel price cap.
newsitem.headline: China says own refiners flout diesel price cap.

text.p: China's State Planning Commission has accused some domestic companies in the oil sector of violating regulations by selling diesel fuel at higher than state-set prices, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
It said that the refiners and filling stations were taking advantage of strong demand and supply shortages to push up domestic prices beyond authorised levels.
The report by the official news agency did not name any of the companies and did not threaten any punitive action.

The State Planning Commission sets prices for diesel fuel -- as well as some other essential commodities -- though China has tried to let market forces determine prices of a growing number of goods in recent years.
Refiners have said that state-set diesel price levels left them with insufficient profits.
China raised domestic diesel prices twice in the fourth quarter of last year to try to ease the financial burden on refiners.

Xinhua said that state prices were being ignored by refiners and gas stations in the southern provinces of Guangdong and Hunan as well as southwestern Yunnan and Sichuan, eastern Shandong and northwestern Ningxia.
Diesel prices of some filling stations in Yunnan province were 1,100 yuan ($132) per tonne higher than the state price, the agency said without giving further details.
The report said that in future the State Planning Commission would publicly announce its diesel price limits for 35 cities. The price levels are known in the trade but are not formally made public.
Chinas' diesel production rose 11 percent in 1996 to 43.25 million tonnes.
China produced 3.845 million tonnes of diesel in January of this year, up 12 percent from the same month of 1996, the State Statistical Bureau said.
